legend: Monotonous round nuclei with a regular nuclear membrane, uniformly granular chromatin, and absent to inconspicuous nucleoli are diagnostic of low-grade nuclear atypia.

Core biopsies of radiologically detected microcalcifications show cystically dilated ducts with luminal mucin and calcifications. Occasional ducts show cytoarchitectural atypia with rigid arches and delicate micropapillae formed by a monotonous epithelial population, consistent with atypical ductal hyperplasia. It is generally recommended that caution is exercised in core biopsy material, unless the extent or size of the changes exceeds the threshold for atypical ductal hyperplasia, upon which a diagnosis of low grade DCIS may be made.
